semantic_reason: Paid dungeon room expansion has independently persisted spatial occupancy/frontier and unique-special-room consumed history, used by actual server key-gated generation. Not an alchemy/altar input or crystal progress clone, not world player SoulNetwork account, not a player Clone field; wrapper, helpers, door kinds, lists and room instances are one chain, one credit.
observations: Controller deserialize creates fresh DungeonSynthesizer, delegates read and rebinds actual TileDungeonController; absent payload also creates a new empty synthesizer. serialize owns nested controller compound.

Synthesizer saves JSON door-type/direction/position frontier, NBT rectangular occupied areas, buffered special pool IDs and placements-since-special map. AreaDescriptor rectangle reads exact six bounds; Serializers supplies Direction and BlockPos readers. No scalar player progress ownership implied.

Normal addNewRoom tries10 random placements then connective corridor fallback. Success0 consumes one actual key in controller; corridor fallback1 and complete failure2 do not consume. Predesignated placement consumes key if true but returns1 regardless; return value is not a generic paid receipt.

Random placement uses saved descriptor intersections and build-height guard. Attempt commits descriptors/structure, increments transient activatedDoors, checks special registry eligibility, updates frontier and seals. Dirty tracking is through controller setChanged on successful main route.

Special removal consumes buffered pool and adds tracker entry0; registry excludes both buffered and tracker-contained pools before evaluating room-count/depth predicate. This is a durable unique special-room exclusion receipt, not merely a display counter.

activatedDoors is not written/read; constructor resets0. Thus persisted special-room exclusions survive but total-room eligibility count is not fully preserved. Do not copy this omission into Dynasty permanent progression.

Reader assumes fresh instance: appends descriptors/buffer and puts tracker entries without clearing reused collections. JSON parsing, Direction byName, ResourceLocation construction and bounds reads lack full malformed-input validation. Rotation failure uses labeled break to abort all rotations; existing forced route does not newly append descriptors here.

No crash atomicity, saved-world correctness, complete registry fallback, loot payout or native playthrough guarantee is inferred. This study informs world-owned persisted facts vs player Clone whitelists only.
